primitives.name: In-Scope File Partition Function
primitives.verbatim_quote: ## Summary table | Branch | Last commit | Ahead / behind main | Files changed vs main (all) | In-scope files (`packages/prediction-engine`, `intelligence`, `packages/ingestion-pipeline`) | Differs from main in a way motif does not have?
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'F_{\\text{in-scope}}(b)': 'set of files under specified packages touched by branch b'}
primitives.assumptions: Only files within `packages/prediction-engine`, `intelligence`, and `packages/ingestion-pipeline` are considered relevant for GSI/GSE integration.
primitives.breakdown_regime: If F_in-scope(b) ≠ ∅, then branch b contributes novel logic to core systems.

layer2.mapping: Used in GSE to compute state transitions based on which modules are modified by each branch.
layer2.telemetry: Count of unique in-scope files per branch.

primitives.name: Motif Consistency Verification
primitives.verbatim_quote: - Blob-SHA check on all 38 in-scope paths touched by any branch below: `motif` blob == `main` blob on every one (checked directly as 38 main-vs-motif pairs, and again across the 59 branch×path rows below).
primitives.symbol_and_unit_ledger: {'\\mathcal{C}(m, \\text{motif})': 'consistency predicate over main and motif SHA hashes'}
primitives.assumptions: SHA equality implies no divergence between main and motif for all in-scope paths.
primitives.breakdown_regime: When \mathcal{C}(m, \text{motif}) = true, motif is consistent with main for tracked files.

layer2.mapping: Enables GSI to validate that motif state aligns with main before applying updates.
layer2.telemetry: Boolean result of SHA comparison across 38 paths.

reasoning_traces.think:
The core insight is that Git merge-base semantics provide a formalized method for comparing branch states against main. This enables precise identification of divergent files through SHA-based consistency checks. The in-scope partition function filters these differences to only those affecting key system components—prediction engine, ingestion pipeline, and intelligence layers. These primitives form a dual structure: one for detecting change (differential), another for validating consistency (motif check). The failure mode arises when a branch modifies an in-scope file without updating motif, leading to inconsistent model states. The GSI layer leverages this to detect drift in predictive models, while GSE uses it to manage state transitions in its reasoning engine.
